text:
maria: proposing a 'targeted override approval pipeline' for runtime config overrides that touch routing/quotas. Goals: safe fast rollouts, auditable approvals, TTLs/auto-expiry, and ops safety hooks. want input from api/console/telemetry/ops.

alex: +1. we need clear scope semantics. A small change to a single tenant should be low friction; global quota bumps must require multi-approver. also enforce an approver group per team.

tess: console UX: show pending overrides in a banner and in the config page with a compact diff + Approve / Reject buttons. require a short reason and suggested TTL (dropdown). show impacted tenants + estimated cost delta.

jun: API proposal (rough):
```json
POST /v1/configs/:config_id/overrides
{
  "scope": { "tenants": ["tenant-a","tenant-b"], "percent": 0.01 },
  "changes": { "route_weight": {"from": 0.2, "to": 0.3}, "quota": {"from": 1000, "to": 2000} },
  "ttl_seconds": 86400,
  "requester": "maria",
  "reason": "experiment + fallback"
}
```
Fields: scope, changes, ttl_seconds, requester, reason. API returns override_id and approval_state.

sahil: telemetry: tag any requests served under an override with override_id and override_source. capture a pre/post snapshot (qps, lat, error) at approval time. also emit an "override.approval" event with approver id and diff. ops alert if >5% error delta in 10m.

kevin: concern — approval fatigue. propose threshold-based shortcuts: auto-approve if scope.tenants <= 3 OR scope.percent < 0.001 AND quota change < 5%. anything above gets queued for human approval.

maria: agree on thresholds, but we should carve exceptions: e.g., routing weight changes that affect global primary routes always require manual approval. default TTL 24h for quick rollbacks.

ops-bot: autosafety: if an override causes error-rate delta > 5% or latency p50 increase > 20% within 10m, trigger automatic revert job and notify #incidents + on-call. Can we capture a small canary sample before full-scope apply?

alex: i'll draft a short RFC + example API & storage model. POC branch next week.

tess: i'll do 2 quick console mocks: one for single-tenant override flow and one for multi-tenant diff view. need sample tenant metadata to show names and estimated token cost.

jun: add an "escalate" button for on-call during business hours that bypasses normal queue but logs action and requires a post-hoc blameless summary.

sahil: question: should approvers be able to extend TTL? i vote yes, but require re-approval if extension > 7d. also keep an extension history.

maria: decision checklist to finalize: (1) numeric thresholds for auto-approve, (2) default TTL 24h, max extension without re-approval 7d, (3) auto-revert safety hook thresholds, (4) API payload/response shape, (5) console UX acceptance flow and reason required, (6) telemetry events and fields. owners: @alex api, @tess console, @sahil telemetry, @jun ops.

kevin: sgtm :+1:

maria: thanks all — i'll file the RFC with these decision points and tag owners. will link RFC here once created.

alex: FYI: thinking about a lightweight approval queue UI in console that surfaces only overrides needing action for each approver group. reduces noise.

tess: nice, that plus an email/digest for pending approvals could help.

maria: cool — leaving this open for 48h for more feedback, then i'll file.

kevin: quick nit — add a small confirmation modal on approve that shows possible rollback command so approvers know how to revert.

maria: good call. adding to RFC.
